new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-press/src/sanitized_save.rs:480-482, 554-557 (covered = whole object span); src/reader.rs:199-218 (span = dict start .. after endstream); src/filters.rs:139 (Flate), :370-371 (ASCIIHex '>'), :407 (ASCII85 '~'), :452 (RunLength 128), :294 (LZW 257); src/syntax.rs:185-188 (comments skipped); src/writer.rs:159-160 (verbatim copy)
new_findings.evidence: When a stream decodes, every raw hit inside its object span is discarded. Only the object-model strings and the decoder output are scanned. Every decoder stops at its end-of-data mark and ignores later bytes. miniz_oxide 0.9.1 decompress_to_vec_inner returns Ok on TINFLStatus::Done without checking that the input is consumed (inflate/mod.rs:225-228). Comments in the stream dictionary are not objects. Example: an object '<< /Filter /ASCIIHexDecode /Length 15 >> stream 41>SECRET-ALPHA endstream' is copied verbatim by save_full. It could also be zlib(x)+'SECRET-ALPHA', or '<< /Length n % SECRET-ALPHA >>'. The proof decodes 'A', drops the raw hit as covered, and is_proven() is true while the removed string sits in the saved file as plain bytes. This contradicts the module doc :3-4 ('every raw byte') and the DESCRIPTOR proof.scope ('comments').
new_findings.remediation: Cover only the encoded bytes the decoder consumed; scan dict text and post-EOD bytes raw (or refuse trailing data typed)

new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-press/src/raster.rs:61, 80-82 (Searchable = never decoded); src/sanitized_save.rs:487-494 (Searchable is a no-op, Raster is listed without decode_prefix/hidden_zlib); src/content.rs:56-93 (inline data stays encoded in the op span)
new_findings.evidence: The proof never decodes inline-image data. An image XObject with /FlateDecode is decoded and scanned. 'BI /W 4 /H 3 /CS /G /BPC 8 /F /Fl ID <zlib of SECRET-ALPHA> EI' is classed Searchable and scanned only in encoded form, so it gives no hit and does not block. The same holds for /F /AHx (hex of the needle) and /F [/Fl /DCT] around a zlib payload (the R6 class-2 fix covers XObjects only). The needle survives in decoded image data and is_proven() is true. The DESCRIPTOR proof.scope claims 'inline-image data' is scanned.
new_findings.remediation: Decode inline-image data through its implemented filters (+hidden_zlib on a raster tail) and scan it; decode failure blocks

new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-press/src/sanitized_save.rs:484 (ops only for kept_streams||is_ap; bd8533f :371 parsed every content-looking stream), :486-513 (inline classification, show_text_ops, opaque and mapped-text checks live inside `if let Some(list) = &ops`)
new_findings.evidence: c520095 fixed the collision exemption by not parsing stray streams at all. That also turned off the opaque-text rule, the ToUnicode mapped-text check and the inline-image Blocking check for every stream that is neither kept nor an appearance. Example: a catalog-reachable stray /Subtype /Form with its own /Resources draws Type0 text without /ToUnicode. At 023c817 it is listed and blocks (OpaqueText); at head it is not listed, so the result reads proven. The same stream drawing the needle as Type0 codes WITH a /ToUnicode map is invisible to the byte scan and the mapped text is never read, so it reads proven, although the DESCRIPTOR says ToUnicode text is read and stray streams are payload. An inline image with /F /Crypt in a stray stream no longer blocks.
new_findings.remediation: Parse every content-looking stream for text/opaque/inline checks; use kept_text_streams only for the collision exemption

new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-press/src/show_text.rs:106-114 (current font set only by Tf, no q/Q stack, no gs /Font) vs src/redaction.rs:499-507, :516-519 (redaction restores the font on Q)
new_findings.evidence: The text state, font included, is part of the graphics state that q/Q save and restore (ISO 32000-1 8.4.1, 9.3.1). Example appearance stream: 'BT /F1 12 Tf q /F2 9 Tf Q <0001...> Tj ET'. F1 is Type0 with a /ToUnicode that spells the needle and F2 is simple. A viewer draws with F1, so the needle is visible. The proof and the appearance scan (text_fields.rs:824) read the codes as F2 Latin-1: no mapped text and no opaque flag, so the result reads proven. With F1 lacking a /ToUnicode, the same trick hides opaque text from the OpaqueText rule. ExtGState /Font set through gs is ignored the same way.
new_findings.remediation: Track the font in a q/Q stack (and gs /Font) in show_text_ops, as redaction.rs does; test both routes

new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-press/src/sanitized_save.rs:484 (parse_content(..).ok() -> None); src/show_text.rs:157-160 (parse error -> mapped empty, opaque false); src/content.rs:53 (any stray ')', '}', '>' or ']' is Malformed)
new_findings.evidence: A kept or appearance stream that the strict tokenizer refuses gets no text reading: the opaque, mapped and inline checks are all skipped. Example: an annotation /AP 'BT /F1 12 Tf <codes> Tj ET }' (Type0 + ToUnicode spelling the needle). Tolerant viewers draw the text before the bad token. Press does not parse it, the byte scan sees only glyph codes, and the result reads proven without a TextFieldPolicy. With one, the appearance is judged on raw Latin-1 and kept as clean.
new_findings.remediation: A kept/AP stream that fails to parse must block (typed, e.g. listed as opaque), never skip the text checks

new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-press/src/show_text.rs:175-185 (content_resources maps only forms with their own /Resources), :104 (fonts None -> every Tf is unresolved -> Simple); src/sanitized_save.rs:496
new_findings.evidence: A kept form XObject without its own /Resources uses the inherited page resources, as redaction does (lane slice 2: own or inherited /Resources). new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-motion-js/src/quickjs.rs:609 (ctx.eval_with_options(input.source, ..)), :674-678 (non-exception error -> EngineFailure::Internal); src/provider.rs:281 (Internal -> poison, sticky); src/quickjs_wire.rs:282, :317 (worker Internal crosses the wire as 7 -> Internal); src/profile.rs:686-711 (raw U+0000 accepted inside string literals), :481-512 (and inside comments); rquickjs-core 0.14.0 src/context/ctx.rs:144 (CString::new(src)? -> Error::InvalidString)
new_findings.evidence: A source holding a U+0000 character, e.g. 'var s = "a<NUL>b"; 1' or '1 // <NUL>', passes the default profile validator: InvalidCharacter only catches NUL outside strings and comments. rquickjs then fails CString::new before the engine runs and returns Error::InvalidString, which is not an Exception and not Allocation. classify maps it to EngineFailure::Internal. In worker mode it travels the wire as code 7 and decodes back to Internal. map_failure then poisons the provider permanently: every later evaluation is Unsupported until it is retired. One hostile expression string in a document disables the provider. This is the consequence R3 and R5 failed on (user input -> Internal -> poison) by a route no test covers, and a 3rd FAIL of this lane exhausts the fix budget.
new_findings.remediation: Refuse U+0000 in source before the engine (validator + provider, typed Parse with span); map pre-eval wrapper errors to non-poison

new_findings.evidence: A script can throw Object.create(SyntaxError.prototype) and get ExprErrorCode::Parse with a span taken from a forged stack. This is not a budget class and does not poison, so R5's rule (no script text selects a BUDGET class) holds. Noted only because the DESCRIPTOR maps 'parse' as an engine syntax error.
new_findings.remediation: Optional: map Parse only when the error came from compilation (no user code ran), else Thrown Other

unsafe_review.evidence: Signatures match windows-sys 0.61.2: GetQueuedCompletionStatus out-pointers u32/usize/*mut *mut OVERLAPPED; CreateIoCompletionPort and CreateJobObjectW return null on failure and both are checked (:94-109); the struct pointers passed with size_of::<T>() are initialised locals (:111-123, :133-153, :159-170). The overlapped value is never dereferenced (for job messages it carries a process id). The RAII guard closes the port and the job exactly once (:222-232). On an attach failure the caller kills and reaps the child (quickjs_worker.rs:431-439). Job and port handles are created non-inheritable (null security attributes). lib.rs:44-45 is deny on windows+quickjs and forbid elsewhere; grep finds no other unsafe in src/. new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-motion-js/src/quickjs_worker.rs:505-508 (drain only after the reply), :564-571 (arm_cpu, no drain before the request); src/job_object.rs:199-219
new_findings.evidence: The completion port is drained only after a request. If the kernel posts a PROCESS_MEMORY_LIMIT notice for request N after N's drain (MS Learn: message delivery is not guaranteed), the pooled worker serves request N+1. N+1's drain then sees memory=true, discards its good reply, and reports Budget(Memory) for a script that never hit the cap. The DESCRIPTOR covers missed notices ('never creates a budget denial') but not late ones. Not reproduced; it depends on kernel posting order (UNVERIFIED).
new_findings.remediation: Drain and discard before arming each request; a late notice on an idle worker retires it without charging a script
